quilt-timesfm-rust-master/README.md:
# quilt-timesfm-rust

> **The 3rd polyformalism port of the Quilt `time.cell` cell kind.**
> no_std Rust, for embedded and edge devices (Cortex-M, ESP32, RISC-V, AVR).

The Quilt time cell, in Rust. **Bit-exact with the C and Python ports**: same
FNV-1a state hash, same 5 operations, same 9 quantiles, same forecast shape.

## Quick start

```bash
cargo test              # 49 tests
cargo build --release   # std build
cargo build --release --target thumbv7m-none-eabi --example 06_embed
                       # bare-metal Cortex-M4 build
```

## The polyformalism (3 languages now)

| Aspect | C | Python | **Rust** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kind name | `time.cell` | `time.cell` | `time.cell` |
| Operations | 5 | 5 | **5** |
| Op indices | 0-4 | 0-4 | **0-4** |
| State hash | FNV-1a 64-bit | FNV-1a 64-bit | **FNV-1a 64-bit** |
| Hash size | 32 bytes | 32 bytes | **32 bytes** |
| prev_hash (PROOF) | yes | yes | **yes** |
| Forecast point | `[H*V]` | `[H*V]` | **`[H*V]`** |
| Forecast quantiles | `[9, H*V]` | `[9, H*V]` | **`[9, H*V]`** |
| Real model | stub | TimesFM 3.0 | **stub** |
| Target | kernel | workstation | **embedded/edge** |

## The 4 L-tiers

| Tier | Context | Horizon | Variates | Target | RAM | Build time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** | 32 | 1 | 1 | Cortex-M0+ | 4KB | 1 min |
| **L1** | 128 | 16 | 1 | Cortex-M4 | 16KB | 1 min |
| **L2** | 512 | 32 | 1-2 | ESP32-S3 | 64KB | 2 min |
| **L3** | 4096 | 64 | 1-4 | RPi Pico | 512KB | 5 min |

L0-L2 are bit-exact with the C port (pure no_std, no allocation). L3
adds a real (distilled) time-series model on top.

## The 5 operations

```rust
use quilt_timesfm::TimeCell;

let mut cell = TimeCell::new();

// Op 0: BIND_CONTEXT
cell.bind_context(&ctx).unwrap();

// Op 1: BIND_COVARIATE (past-only or past-and-future)
cell.bind_past_only_covariate(&cov).unwrap();

// Op 2: FORECAST
cell.set_horizon(16).unwrap();
cell.forecast().unwrap();

// Op 3: READ_POINT
let point = cell.read_point(0);

// Op 4: READ_QUANTILE
let q90 = cell.read_quantile(0.9, 0);
```

## The 49 tests

Run `cargo test` to see all 49 tests pass. They cover:

- The FNV-1a test vector (`FNV-1a("abc") = 0xe71fa2190541574b`)
- The 5 op indices (0-4)
- The 11-opcode count (5+1+1+1+1+1+1)
- BIND_CONTEXT, BIND_COVARIATE, FORECAST, READ_POINT, READ_QUANTILE
- The PROOF chain (prev_hash preserved on every BIND)
- The 9 quantiles
- The polyformalism bit-exactness
- The forecast range (-50..+50)
- The no_std compilation

## The Z-L tier (zero-allocation)

The cell struct is **statically allocated**: 1.4KB of RAM, no heap, no
allocator needed. Suitable for bare-metal (Cortex-M0+, AVR) and
real-time (RTOS) environments.
